subject: FRE
label: Grade 02
task: Meet the outcome of every unit in Grade 02 French, and keep one piece of evidence for each.
condition: A 36-week school year, 4 units, a teacher or guide, a learning book or device, and local examples in the local language first with English support.
standard: Each unit: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school. Course pass: no unit at 'Not yet' after one retry, and a pass in SA1 and SA2.

modules.title: Family and friends
modules.intro: In this unit, 'Family and friends', you learn to name family members. Lessons are short and playful, with objects, pictures and talk. You see it, say it, then do it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Family and friends' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: name family members, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: mon pere, ma mere, mon frere, ma soeur. 'Voici mon ami.' Method: Model run for 'Family and friends'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Name family members: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.
steps: Step 1, Learn family words with my. mon père [my father], ma mère [my mother], mon frère [my brother], ma sœur [my sister], mon grand-père, ma grand-mère [my grandfather, my grandmother]. Use mon with masculine nouns and ma with feminine nouns.

Step 2, Introduce your family. Voici ma famille. [Here is my family.] Voici mon frère. Il s'appelle [prénom]. [Here is my brother. His name is (name).] Voici ma sœur. Elle s'appelle [prénom]. [Here is my sister. Her name is (name).] Use il for a boy and elle for a girl.

Step 3, Talk about friends. Voici mon ami et mon amie. [Here are my friend (a boy) and my friend (a girl).] Nous jouons ensemble. [We play together.] Note mon amie: before a vowel sound even a feminine noun takes mon.

Step 4, Short dialogue. Élève A : C'est qui ? [Who is it?] Élève B : C'est ma grand-mère. Elle s'appelle [prénom]. [It is my grandmother. Her name is (name).] Élève A : Elle est gentille ! [She is kind!] Élève B : Oui, je l'aime beaucoup. [Yes, I love her very much.]
Step 5, Fix an error. A child says ma frère. Correction: mon frère, because frère is masculine. Another slip is mon mère; say ma mère. Check the noun first, then choose mon or ma.

Step 6, Your turn: introduce your mother and your brother with their names. Model answer: Voici ma mère. Elle s'appelle [prénom]. Voici mon frère. Il s'appelle [prénom]. [Here is my mother. Her name is (name). Here is my brother. His name is (name).]

modules.title: My school
modules.intro: In this unit, 'My school', you learn to name school objects. Lessons are short and playful, with objects, pictures and talk. You see it, say it, then do it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'My school' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: name school objects, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: 'Mon ecole est grande. J'ai un cartable et une trousse. J'etudie les maths et l'anglais.' Swap in your own words. Method: Model run for 'My school'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Name school objects: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.
steps: Step 1, Name school objects with un or une. un cahier [a notebook], un stylo [a pen], un livre [a book], une règle [a ruler], une trousse [a pencil case], une chaise [a chair], une table [a table]. Point to each and say its name.

Step 2, Ask and answer. Qu'est-ce que c'est ? [What is it?] C'est une règle. [It is a ruler.] C'est un cahier. [It is a notebook.] Ask about five objects in your classroom and answer with C'est un or C'est une.

Step 3, Say where things are. Où est ma trousse ? [Where is my pencil case?] Elle est dans mon sac. [It is in my bag.] Où est mon livre ? [Where is my book?] Il est sur la table. [It is on the table.] Use dans [in], sur [on], sous [under].

Step 4, Learn classroom instructions. Ouvrez vos livres. [Open your books.] Fermez vos cahiers. [Close your notebooks.] Asseyez-vous. [Sit down.] Écoutez, s'il vous plaît. [Listen, please.] Respond with the action and say Oui, madame.

Step 5, Fix an error. A child says C'est un règle. Correction: C'est une règle, because règle is feminine. Another slip is Il est dans mon sac for a trousse; use Elle est dans mon sac, because trousse is feminine.

Step 6, Your turn: say what a ruler is and where your pen is. Model answer: C'est une règle. Mon stylo est sur la table. [It is a ruler. My pen is on the table.] Then give a command: Ouvrez vos cahiers. [Open your notebooks.]

modules.title: Animals and body
modules.intro: In this unit, 'Animals and body', you learn to name animals and body parts. Lessons are short and playful, with objects, pictures and talk. You see it, say it, then do it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Animals and body' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: name animals and body parts, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: un chien, un chat, la tete, le bras, la jambe. 'J'ai mal a la tete.' (I have a headache.) Method: Model run for 'Animals and body'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Name animals and body parts: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.
steps: Step 1, Name animals. le chat [the cat], le chien [the dog], le cheval [the horse], la vache [the cow], l'oiseau [the bird], le poisson [the fish]. Say each one and make its sound or movement.
Step 2, Name body parts. la tête [head], le nez [nose], la bouche [mouth], la main [hand], le pied [foot], les yeux [eyes], les bras [arms], les jambes [legs]. Touch each part as you say it.

Step 3, Describe with avoir. J'ai deux yeux et un nez. [I have two eyes and a nose.] Le chien a quatre pattes. [The dog has four legs.] L'oiseau a deux ailes. [The bird has two wings.] Use a for he or she has.
Step 4, Ask and answer. Tu as un animal ? [Do you have a pet?] Oui, j'ai un chat. Il s'appelle [nom]. [Yes, I have a cat. His name is (name).] Il est petit et noir. [He is small and black.]
Step 5, Fix an error. A child says deux œil. Correction: deux yeux, because œil [eye] has an irregular plural. Another slip is saying the final s in les bras; in les bras the s of bras is silent.

Step 6, Your turn: say your pet has four legs and a long tail, and that you have two hands. Model answer: Mon chien a quatre pattes et une longue queue. J'ai deux mains. [My dog has four legs and a long tail. I have two hands.]

modules.title: Songs and rhymes
modules.intro: In this unit, 'Songs and rhymes', you learn to sing short songs. Lessons are short and playful, with objects, pictures and talk. You see it, say it, then do it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Songs and rhymes' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: sing short songs, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: Au clair de la lune, mon ami Pierrot, prete-moi ta plume. Les mots qui riment: lune et plume. Method: Model run for 'Songs and rhymes'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Sing short songs: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.
steps: Step 1, Learn a short rhyme I made. Un, deux, trois, quatre, je tape des mains. [One, two, three, four, I clap my hands.] Cinq, six, sept, huit, je dis bonjour au matin. [Five, six, seven, eight, I say hello to the morning.] Clap on each number.

Step 2, Work out the meaning line by line. je tape des mains means I clap my hands. je dis bonjour means I say hello. au matin means in the morning. Mime each action slowly, then say the line again with a steady beat.

Step 3, Notice the rhyme. mains and matin end with a similar sound, the nasal in. Other pairs with the same sound: main and pain, chien and bien. Say each pair twice, making the sound come through the nose.

Step 4, Perform in two groups. Group A sings Un, deux, trois, quatre, je tape des mains. Group B answers Cinq, six, sept, huit, je dis bonjour au matin. Then everyone sings both lines together, faster each time.

Step 5, Fix an error. A child says the s in mains and the t is dropped in huit. Correction: in mains the s is silent, but in huit you hear the t, so say weet. Count again from un to dix with correct sounds.

Step 6, Your turn: make a second verse with the days using the same tune. Model answer: Lundi, mardi, je saute bien. Mercredi, jeudi, je chante bien. [Monday, Tuesday, I jump well. Wednesday, Thursday, I sing well.]

rubric: Explains the idea to someone else

ladder: L1: say and read familiar words and short sentences.
L2: read short texts and write connected sentences.
L3: write paragraphs and speak on a topic with notes.
L4: write for different purposes and analyse how texts persuade.
L5: write and argue at length; handle unseen texts.
L6 (degree): academic reading, writing and citation.
L7 (postgraduate): publish, teach or translate with expert accuracy.
